newsitem.title: UK: LIFFE coffee loses further momentum as offers buil.
newsitem.headline: LIFFE coffee loses further momentum as offers buil.

text.p: Origin selling and speculative profit-taking knocked London robusta futures further in the afternoon to end Wednesday sharply down.

Traders said the market also took little heed from relatively stable New York arabica prices which rose at one stage on news dockworkers at Colombia's key Buenaventura port threathened to go on strike.
Robusta was overwhelmed by selling orders from the origins.
"The producers thought it would be timely to sell at these prices," said one trader. "Speculators who had been chasing the market up also decided to take profits."
Traders said the slide was also exacerbated by a dearth of manufacturer interest. Roaster interest had been evident in the past two days.
But volume at 4,669 lots, which include active July/Sept switches, was far from impressive.
By the finish, benchmark May stood $41 down at $1,657 a tonne after ranging between $1,700 and $1,653. Other positions were $20 to $36 down.
Immediately, market players will keep a watch on Thursday's Association of Coffee Producing Countries (ACPC) technical group meeting in London although no major decision is expected.
The meeting is expected to analyse the recent sharp hike in world coffee prices and its impact on consumption.
The technical group is made up of Brazil, Colombia, Indonesia, Ivory Coast, El Salvador and Uganda.

The possible Colombian dockworkers' strike, which could begin in less than a month if no deal is reached, is being threatened in protest at port operators's failure to fulfill the terms of an accord hammered out in January. -- Jalil Hamid, London newsroom +44 171 542 4985
